summary.answer:
**A1 has 1,902 customers, which is 79% of the 2,396 customers in Texas.**

| | Customers | Area (km²) | Customers per 10,000 km² |
|---|---|---|---|
| Inside A1 | 1,902 | ~147,000 | ~129 |
| Rest of Texas | 494 | ~549,000 | ~9 |

A1 covers about 21% of Texas but holds about 4 out of 5 of its customers. Customers are packed about **14 times more densely** there than in the rest of the state.

**Why so many there:** A1 is the "Texas Triangle", which takes in four of the state's biggest metro areas:
- **Houston:** 355 customers
- **San Antonio:** 188
- **Dallas–Fort Worth:** Fort Worth 103, Dallas 101, Arlington 59, Plano 39, Garland 27, and more
- **Austin:** 97

The customer data seems to follow where people live, so the cluster reflects the region's population rather than something unusual about the store. In real life the Triangle holds roughly 70% of Texans, so this dataset is even a bit more concentrated there than the population is.

I counted customers whose home location is inside the Texas state boundary and checked each one against A1.

run.prompt:
How many customers are inside A1 and how does it compare to the rest of Texas?

Map annotations drawn by the user (refer to them by id; geojson is [lon, lat], usable with ST_GEOGFROMGEOJSON):
- A1 "why so many here?": Polygon, bbox [-99, 29, -94.7, 33.4], ~146,557 km²
  geojson: {"type":"Polygon","coordinates":[[[-97.6,33.4],[-96,33.3],[-94.7,30.2],[-94.9,29.3],[-95.6,29],[-98.9,29],[-99,29.8],[-97.6,33.4]]]}

tools.name: run_sql

input.sql:
WITH a AS (SELECT ST_GEOGFROMGEOJSON('{"type":"Polygon","coordinates":[[[-97.6,33.4],[-96,33.3],[-94.7,30.2],[-94.9,29.3],[-95.6,29],[-98.9,29],[-99,29.8],[-97.6,33.4]]]}') g),
tx AS (SELECT state_geom FROM `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.states` WHERE state_name='Texas')
SELECT ST_INTERSECTS(ST_GEOGPOINT(u.longitude,u.latitude), a.g) inside, COUNT(*) n,
 ROUND(ST_AREA(ANY_VALUE(IF(ST_INTERSECTS(ST_GEOGPOINT(u.longitude,u.latitude), a.g), ST_INTERSECTION(a.g, tx.state_geom), ST_DIFFERENCE(tx.state_geom, a.g))))/1e6) km2
FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.users` u, a, tx
WHERE ST_INTERSECTS(ST_GEOGPOINT(u.longitude,u.latitude), tx.state_geom)
GROUP BY 1
